sections.title: Basic Concept
sections.content: A dice or cube has 6 faces. Each face may contain a number, letter, or symbol. The main goal in dice questions is to identify opposite faces and adjacent faces using given views.

sections.title: Standard Dice Rule
sections.content: In a standard dice, opposite faces always sum to 7. The pairs are (1-6), (2-5), and (3-4). If 1 is on the top, 6 will be at the bottom.

sections.title: Ordinary Dice Concept
sections.content: In an ordinary dice, there is no fixed sum rule. Any two adjacent faces may sum to 7. Always rely on the given positions instead of assuming standard rules.

sections.title: Rule of 1 Common Surface
sections.content: If two different positions of a dice show one common face in the same position, then the other visible faces are adjacent to that common face. The face that does not appear with it will be opposite.

sections.title: Rule of 2 Common Surfaces
sections.content: If two positions show two common faces, then the third changing face in each position will be opposite to each other.

sections.title: Descriptive Position Example
sections.content: Position 1: 1 on top, 2 in front, 3 on right. Position 2: 1 on top, 4 in front, 5 on right. Step 1: 1 is common. Step 2: 2, 3, 4, 5 are adjacent to 1. Step 3: Therefore, 2 is opposite to 4.

sections.title: Cube Cutting Basics
sections.content: If a cube is cut into smaller equal cubes, corner cubes have 3 painted faces, edge cubes have 2 painted faces, face center cubes have 1 painted face, and inner cubes have no painted faces.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Confusing standard and ordinary dice. 2. Mixing up opposite and adjacent faces. 3. Not visualizing rotation properly. 4. Ignoring common surface rules.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Focus on identifying common faces between positions. Remember opposite faces never appear together. In standard dice, opposite faces sum to 7.

tricks.title: Standard Opposite Pair Trick
tricks.explanation: Memorize opposite pairs of standard dice.
tricks.example: If 3 is on top, 4 will be at the bottom.

tricks.title: Three Faces Rule
tricks.explanation: The three faces visible together are always adjacent to each other.
tricks.example: If 1, 2, 3 appear together, they are all adjacent.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: If a number appears with four different numbers in different views, the remaining number is its opposite.
tricks.example: If 1 appears with 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6 is opposite to 1.

tricks.title: Rule of 1 Shortcut
tricks.explanation: When one face is common in two views, compare the changing faces to find the opposite.
tricks.example: 1 is common; 2 and 4 change positions. So 2 is opposite to 4.

tricks.title: Rule of 2 Shortcut
tricks.explanation: When two faces are common, the third changing faces are opposite.
tricks.example: If 2 and 3 are common and 4 changes to 5, then 4 and 5 are opposite.

tricks.title: Mental Rotation Trick
tricks.explanation: Rotate the dice mentally, not reflect it. Opposite faces can never become adjacent.
tricks.example: If 1 is opposite 6, they can never appear side by side.

tricks.title: Corner Rule in Cube Cutting
tricks.explanation: A cube always has 8 corner cubes.

tricks.title: Quick Painted Face Idea
tricks.explanation: Corner = 3 painted faces, Edge = 2, Face center = 1.
tricks.example: In a 3x3x3 cube, 8 cubes will have 3 painted faces.
